idiom_name: readonly record struct/record with with-expressions, static pure methods and LINQ
implementation_notes: The compiler-generated record machinery replaces the hand-written immutable value class: positional properties of a record class or readonly record struct are init-only, and a with expression produces a copy with selected members changed instead of mutating in place (record struct properties are read-write unless the struct is declared readonly). Static expression-bodied methods over IReadOnlyList/IEnumerable are the query form, and LINQ operators (Where, Select, Sum) return new sequences instead of modifying the source. Keep the classic mutable class for entities with identity and lifecycle, and expose their transitions as commands; note that records, readonly and with are all shallow, so mutable reference-typed members still need copies at the boundary.
pitfalls: with and readonly are shallow: a reference-typed member (List<T>, array) is shared by the copy and can still be mutated through either instance.
LINQ queries are lazy and re-enumerated on each iteration; capturing mutable state or reusing an iterator makes a nominally pure query observably stateful.
DateTime.Now, Random and culture-dependent formatting inside a query are hidden inputs - pass the clock and the culture in as parameters.
